subject: Take colour value from data frame

messages.author: e715a3aeb27b07f3
messages.subject: Take colour value from data frame
parts:
Hello,

I have a data frame which already contains colour values for each data
point and I'd like to display the data points with the given colour.
But how???

Antje

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Take colour value from data frame
parts:
Hi,

here is a minimal example:

d <- data.frame(x=1:3, y=1:3, co=c("green", "pink", "green"))
ggplot(d, aes(x,y,colour=co)) + geom_point() +
scale_colour_manual(value=d$co, breaks=d$co)

--

messages.author: e715a3aeb27b07f3
messages.subject: Re: Take colour value from data frame
parts:
Hi,

here is a little example

library(ggplot2)

row <- 1:10
col <- 1:10
myDF <- expand.grid(row = row, col = col)
myDF$value <- 1:100
myDF$colIv <- cut(myDF$value, breaks = seq(0,100,2))

my.colors <- c("blue",rainbow(48),"green")

p <- ggplot(myDF, aes(x = col, y = row, fill = colIv)) + geom_tile()
p <- p + scale_fill_manual(values = my.colors)
p

The legend I get is pretty long and using my real data it slows down
the plot. If I don't plot the legend it's fine. A colour scale bar
would be nice in this case (something like this:
http://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/fx_files/2558/2/colorscales.png
)

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Take colour value from data frame
parts:
Hi,

yes, scale_*_identity does this.

As for the matlab type colormap (colorbar), now I'm just on the way to
implement that for my own use.
Generally, colormap cannot work with discrete scale, so maybe it is
not available for your case (even in matlab? i don't know matlab is
sensitive to if the variable is discrete or continuous).

I attached the example code and output, but the current state is very
very ad-hoc and hence is even far from alpha, and I'm not sure this
feature is merged in the future release.
If many people want this feature, and Hadley are considering to merge
this kind of feature, then maybe I will try to make a progress on this
feature.

# note that this code cannot work with current version of ggplot2
d <- data.frame(x=1:100, y=runif(100), fi=runif(100))
ggplot(d, aes(x,y,colour=fi, size=fi)) + geom_point() +
scale_colour_continuous(colorbar=TRUE)
colorbar=TRUE works for scale_fill or scale_color (maybe also scale_alpha?)

--

messages.author: e715a3aeb27b07f3
messages.subject: Re: Take colour value from data frame
parts:
Nice feature :-) I would like to see it implemented in the future...

I just went for the discrete scale because I could not find any way to
apply customized colours on a continuous scale (exactly defining
colors for given intervals). In the end, color mapping is nothing else
than mapping discrete values ( colours) to intervals of continuous
values, no?
I don't use Matlab at all, I just sent this link to make sure that you
know what I'm looking for.

For now, I use a simple solution - creating a colorbar as additional plot:

library(ggplot2)
my.colors <- c("blue",rainbow(48),"green")

myDF <- expand.grid(row = row, col = col)
myDF$value <- 1:100
myDF$colIv <- my.colors[unclass(cut(myDF$value, breaks = seq(0,100,2)))]
myDF$meta <- "data"

scaleDF <- data.frame(col = 1, row = 1:50, colIv = my.colors, meta =
"scalebar", value = NA)

myDF <- rbind(myDF,scaleDF)
p <- ggplot(myDF, aes(x = col, y = row, fill = colIv)) + geom_tile()

p <- p + scale_fill_identity()
p <- p + facet_wrap( ~ meta , scales = "free_y")
p <- p + opts(legend.position = "none")
p


Antje
